title: What Is Risk Per Trade?
hook: A 30-point stop is not a $30 loss.

launchpad.outcome: Turn a stop distance into approximate dollar risk: points × $ per point × contracts.
launchpad.missionQuestion: How much am I actually risking?

lines: You know how to take a trade.
But can your account survive the way you’re taking them?
KNOW THE LOSS BEFORE YOU CHASE THE PROFIT.

slides.heading: Entry 20,000 · Stop 19,970
slides.punch: PRICE RISK = the distance between entry and stop.

slides.heading: The formula
slides.punch: = APPROXIMATE PRICE RISK, before fees and slippage.

slides.title: Same chart stop. Different account exposure.

options.feedback: That’s the points, read as dollars.

slides.punch: A 30-POINT STOP IS NOT A $30 LOSS.

slides.prompt: What three things decide your dollar risk?
slides.modelAnswer: The stop distance in points, the dollar value per point of the instrument, and how many contracts. Together they give the approximate price risk, before fees and slippage.

remember: A 30-point stop is not a $30 loss.
